title: EPIC CR-1: one-market continuous runtime
description:
CR-1 means one operator-selected active-program market at S=12 may repeat
maker-entry, reduction, flat and requote cycles without synchronous operator
involvement during one declared market assignment. It runs under launchd and
caffeinate, survives process and websocket restarts through safe adoption, and
either continues safely or durably enters WINDING_DOWN while reduction,
monitoring, heartbeat and alert retry remain alive.

The closed operating envelope is: one selected ticker; dedicated account with
only declared capital and no unrelated cash, positions, orders or manual
activity; manual market replacement; no claim of automatic programme rotation.
Required evidence is a event-complete read-only qualification, clean balance-derived S<=12 first-fill
stage, clean attended repeated-cycle evidence, final scenario/invariant and operational
readiness, exact candidate checks under the faster verification workflow, active external dead man, and explicit
operator review.

New work blocks CR-1 only after adjudication that its failure is reachable in
this operating envelope or that CR-1 acceptance cannot be evidenced without it.
Priority labels alone do not move the finish line. Dynamic selection, rotation
and automatic management of unrelated held markets belong to CR-2; CR-1 instead
refuses a dirty account and stops on foreign activity.

Acceptance: record exact commit, config/rung, assignment window, dedicated-
account check, supervision state, runbook/drill evidence and links to all three
promotion rungs. After closure, repeated cycles are authorised only inside that
assignment.

title: CR-1 operations: recovery, disk headroom, runbook, and alert escalation
description:
CR-1 is authorised for unattended repeated cycles inside one declared market
assignment. Before that authorization, make the operational recovery boundary
executable rather than implicit.

Deliver one concise operator runbook and its tested software checks: dedicated
account cleanliness; config/commit/rung confirmation; disk headroom and bounded
store/evidence growth; durable-latch stop/resume; recovery when the harness
store is unreadable while exchange orders or inventory may exist; disposition
of every SEV1/SEV2; and escalation when a SEV1 or missed heartbeat is not
acknowledged. No procedure may clear a latch or infer flatness from unavailable
truth.

This is one operational-readiness unit, not one bead per checklist row. It does
not run the live harness; operator drills and evidence remain operator actions.

The runbook names exact commands, preconditions, stop conditions and evidence
for normal start, planned stop, latched restart, corrupt/unreadable store,
insufficient disk headroom, missed heartbeat and unacknowledged SEV1. Automated
tests prove unsafe states refuse or enter durable WINDING_DOWN while reduction
and observation continue wherever authoritative truth permits. The final CR-1
evidence links a completed operator drill for the external escalation path.

title: CR-2: manage held non-selected markets across rotation
description:
CR-2, not the one-market pilot, owns dynamic management when complete account
truth contains positions or live orders outside the currently selected ticker.
Implement the H-ORD-5b expansion only with selection/rotation semantics: derive
the managed set from authoritative truth, subscribe and maintain required books,

foreign order.

CR-1 instead binds a dedicated clean-account precondition and refuses startup
or durably stops on foreign activity. Do not pull this work back onto the CR-1
path without a new operating-envelope decision.

remain untouched. Multi-market caps, P&L, schedule and monitor evidence remain
complete. A selected-only mutation is caught by a composed scenario. This bead
does not block q01, the S=1 canary, S=12 burn-in or one-market CR-1.

title: rest: Fills() walks all account history every call; backfill_h is client-side
description: harness/rest/read.go Fills() does a COMPLETE cursor walk then filters by `since` client-side. That is correct per H-PAGE-1 clause 2 (a server-side early stop on timestamp would make the walk incomplete, and only a complete walk may replace state), and it is fine for the pilot: 15 fills on the account, one market, days. It does not scale — at a 5s poll over months the walk grows without bound. Options when it matters: (a) measure whether /portfolio/fills honours min_ts and whether a bounded read still counts as complete for its window, (b) keep a durable high-water mark in harness.db and walk only until the first already-seen fill_id, treating THAT as the completeness criterion. Neither is safe to assume; both need the V1.8a treatment (measure, record, then code).
notes: 2026-09-26 authenticated min_ts experiment over15 retained fills/one page matched inclusive boundaries at oldest and newest exact timestamp and +/-1s (nine probes); complete evidence account-selected.json. Small single-page retained history cannot establish boundary-tie/multi-page/concurrent-arrival or historical-retention completeness. Exhaustive production walk preserved; performance optimization remains deferred evidence work, not a blocker for this small account.
